mission.name: Lost in the Maze
mission.description: The billing service needs its vault access code, but nobody remembers where the old admin left secret.conf. The sandbox is a copy of the server's directory tree.
mission.objective: Find the file named exactly secret.conf and write the value of its access_code setting (only the value, without 'access_code=') to answer.txt in the sandbox root

mission.name: Build the Scaffold
mission.description: A web app refuses to start because the directories it writes to do not exist yet. Someone already created data/ by hand and put customer notes in it.
mission.objective: Create the directories logs/app, logs/nginx, data/uploads, data/cache/thumbnails and tmp/sessions inside the sandbox. The existing data/README must stay untouched.

mission.name: Spring Cleaning
mission.description: A crashed batch job left temporary .tmp files all over the build server. Some sit in hidden folders, some have spaces in their names, and the templates folder holds .tmpl files that are still in use.
mission.objective: Delete every file whose name ends in .tmp anywhere in the sandbox, and nothing else

mission.name: The Great Migration
mission.description: Release 4.2 was unpacked into staging/ instead of production/. Before installing it you must keep a copy of the live app config, so you can roll back.
mission.objective: 1) Copy production/app.conf to production/app.conf.old. 2) Move every .conf file from staging/ into production/. 3) Move staging/app.conf.new to production/app.conf. Afterwards only notes.txt may remain in staging/.

mission.name: Needle in a Haystack
mission.description: A developer is moving to a new laptop and needs a list of every Python file they wrote, spread over three projects and a hidden virtualenv.
mission.objective: Write the path of every regular file whose name ends in .py, one per line, to found.txt in the sandbox root (relative paths like ./project-a/x.py or absolute paths are both fine)

mission.name: The Password Leak
mission.description: A security scan flagged this repository: someone hardcoded passwords in plain text. Security needs the full list of affected files before anyone rotates credentials.
mission.objective: Write the path of every file that contains the text password= (lowercase, exactly that), one per line, to leak.txt in the sandbox root

mission.name: The Shortcut
mission.description: myapp always reads etc/myapp/active.conf, which is a symlink to the config version in use. Version 2 is approved, but the link still points at version 1. The myapp folder gets copied to other servers, so absolute links would break there.
mission.objective: Make etc/myapp/active.conf a relative symlink that points to v2/config.conf in the same folder. Do not copy, move or edit the config files.

mission.name: Pack and Unpack
mission.description: The website backup arrived as backup.tar.gz and has to be restored for inspection. Support also wants the current log files, compressed, but not the rotated or non-log files in that folder.
mission.objective: Extract backup.tar.gz into a new extracted/ directory (so extracted/site/index.html exists), then create a gzip-compressed archive.tar.gz in the sandbox root that contains exactly the files in logs/ whose names end in .log

mission.name: Disk Hog
mission.description: The server disk is 97% full. Before deleting anything, the team lead wants to know which single file takes the most space; the biggest folder is not necessarily where it is.
mission.objective: Write the path of the single largest file in the sandbox (one line, relative like ./dir/file or absolute) to biggest.txt in the sandbox root

mission.name: Secrets in Plain Sight
mission.description: The deploy pipeline needs the app's AUTH_TOKEN. The app keeps it in a hidden file under a hidden config folder, so a plain ls shows nothing useful.
mission.objective: Find the hidden file that holds the real AUTH_TOKEN and write only its value (the text after AUTH_TOKEN=) to token.txt in the sandbox root. .env.example is a template with a placeholder, not the real token.

mission.name: Log Triage
mission.description: The payment service crashed overnight and left a 3,000-line app.log. The on-call engineer wants to see how it started up and how it died, without scrolling through all of it.
mission.objective: Write exactly the first 5 lines of app.log to first5.txt and exactly the last 5 lines to last5.txt

mission.name: Error Extraction
mission.description: Ops is writing the post-mortem for last night's outage. They need every ERROR and FATAL line from a 2,500-line app.log, in their original order, and nothing else.
mission.objective: Save all lines of app.log that contain ERROR or FATAL (uppercase, as the log level is written) to errors.txt, in the same order as in app.log

mission.name: By the Numbers
mission.description: The product team wants three numbers from yesterday's web server log (access.log, nginx combined format): how many requests, from how many different clients, and how much data was sent.
mission.objective: Create report.txt with exactly these three lines: requests=<number of requests>, unique_ips=<number of distinct client IPs>, bytes=<total response bytes>. The response size is the number right after the status code; '-' means 0 bytes.

mission.name: Top Talkers
mission.description: The shop's API slowed down this morning and security suspects a few clients are hammering it. They want a ranking of client IPs by number of requests in access.log.
mission.objective: Write top_ips.txt with one line per client IP in the form '<count> <ip>' (the format uniq -c prints), every IP from access.log listed exactly once, highest count first

mission.name: Find and Replace
mission.description: The app is moving from staging to production. Its config.conf still points at hosts in the staging.internal domain; production uses prod.internal. The staging file itself must stay as it is.
mission.objective: Create config.prod.conf: a copy of config.conf in which every occurrence of staging.internal is replaced by prod.internal and nothing else changes. config.conf must stay unchanged.

mission.name: Column Harvest
mission.description: Billing needs a contact list for invoices. The user export users.csv has a header row and five columns (username,age,email,role,status), but billing only charges users whose status is active.
mission.objective: Create extract.csv with one line 'username,email' for every user whose status is exactly active, in the same order as users.csv, with no header line

mission.name: Pipeline Master
mission.description: Someone is flooding the shop with fake orders. The API team wants to know which clients send the most POST requests (orders and cart writes) according to access.log. The docs pages have POST in their URLs, and crawlers read them all day.
mission.objective: Write post_ips.txt with one line '<count> <ip>' per client that sent at least one POST request (count = its number of POST requests), highest count first. Only requests whose HTTP method is POST count.

mission.name: Spot the Difference
mission.description: Release 4.2 changes the shop-api config. Before the change goes out, the reviewers want it as a patch they can read and apply with the patch tool on the servers that still run v1.conf.
mission.objective: Save the differences from v1.conf (old) to v2.conf (new) as a unified diff in changes.diff, so that applying changes.diff to v1.conf produces v2.conf. Leave v1.conf and v2.conf unchanged.

mission.name: Script Won't Run
mission.description: A teammate uploaded deploy.sh to the release folder, but running ./deploy.sh fails with 'Permission denied'.
mission.objective: Make deploy.sh executable for its owner (without making it writable by group or others), then run it as ./deploy.sh so it writes output.txt

mission.name: Octal Surgery
mission.description: Someone 'fixed' a web app by running chmod 777 on everything. Now anyone on the server can rewrite the code and read the database password.
mission.objective: Using numeric (octal) modes: index.html readable by everyone but writable only by you; app.py readable and runnable by everyone but writable only by you; secrets.conf readable and writable by you and nobody else

mission.name: Who Owns This?
mission.description: A deploy failed with 'Operation not permitted' while changing permissions on a list of paths. Before asking an admin for help, work out who owns each path and which ones you are allowed to change yourself.
mission.objective: For every path in paths.txt write a line '<path> <owner> <group>' to owners.txt. Then write to fixable.txt (one per line) only the paths from paths.txt that you own, because only a file's owner (or root) can chmod, chgrp or chown it

mission.name: Shared Space
mission.description: The team's shared/ upload folder is writable by everyone, which is intended. The problem: anyone can also delete or rename everyone else's uploads, and files keep disappearing.
mission.objective: Keep shared/ readable, writable and enterable by everyone (rwx for all), but make it so users can only delete or rename their own files in it. Don't remove any of the uploads

mission.name: The Audit Trail
mission.description: After a break-in, the security team suspects the attacker planted programs with the SUID or SGID bit so they can regain higher privileges later. The copied server tree is in this sandbox.
mission.objective: Find every regular file in the sandbox that has the SUID or SGID bit set and write their paths to suid_files.txt, one per line (./bin/x or full paths both work). Directories don't count, and nothing else may be listed

mission.name: Default Lockdown
mission.description: The report app's start script sets a umask that makes every file it creates world-writable, and the reports it has already written are exposed too.
mission.objective: Fix the umask in start_app.sh so everything it creates from now on is 640 (files) and 750 (directories). Then make sure the existing data/ tree has those same modes

mission.name: Web Server 403
mission.description: After a site was restored from a backup, nginx answers 403 Forbidden for every page. The web server runs as a different user, and the restore left webroot/ private to you.
mission.objective: In webroot/ (including webroot itself and every subfolder): all directories must be 755 and all files 644. Hidden files and names with spaces count too, and no file may be deleted

mission.name: World Writable Files
mission.description: A security scan flagged world-writable files in the app/ directory: any user on the server could change them. The team relies on the other permission bits (some files are group-writable or executable on purpose).
mission.objective: Remove write permission for 'others' from every world-writable file under app/, and change nothing else: owner and group bits must stay as they are, and no file may be deleted

mission.name: Process Detective
mission.description: The server feels slow and the fans are loud. One of the jobs started from this sandbox is burning CPU, hidden among the other processes.
mission.objective: Save the 5 processes using the most CPU (ps output with PID, %CPU and command, highest first) to top_procs.txt, and the PID of the runaway sandbox job to culprit.txt

mission.name: Runaway Process
mission.description: Someone left debug_logger.sh running: it appends to debug.log every second and is slowly filling the disk. web_server.sh, started from the same folder, is serving customers and must stay up.
mission.objective: Stop the debug_logger.sh process. web_server.sh must keep running

mission.name: The Background Worker
mission.description: process.sh crunches today's data and takes a while. You don't want your terminal blocked while it runs, and the team lead wants proof that it was running as a job of your shell.
mission.objective: Start process.sh as a background job. While it is still running, save your shell's job list, with PIDs, to jobs.txt. Then wait for the job to finish so it writes result.txt

mission.name: Play Nice
mission.description: A CPU-heavy batch job, heavy.sh, is already running and competing with the services users depend on. It has done half its work, so restarting it is not an option.
mission.objective: Lower the priority of the running heavy.sh process to niceness 15, without stopping or restarting it

mission.name: Signal Relay
mission.description: Support needs debug logs from the listener service, which is running right now. Like most daemons, it re-reads its config file when it receives SIGHUP. Restarting it would drop every connected client.
mission.objective: Change log_level in listener.conf from info to debug, then make the running listener load the new config without stopping or restarting it. listener.status shows what the running service is using

mission.name: Zombie Apocalypse
mission.description: Monitoring reports defunct (zombie) processes piling up. A buggy program in this sandbox starts workers and never collects their exit status. Another sandbox program, metrics_agent.py, is healthy and must keep running.
mission.objective: Save the PIDs of the zombie processes to zombies.txt (one per line; extra columns like PPID or name are fine). Then stop the parent process that is failing to reap them, and only that one

mission.name: Speak Variable
mission.description: The onboarding script greet.sh is supposed to greet whoever runs it, but nobody ever got past the TODO comment.
mission.objective: Make `bash greet.sh NAME` print `Hello, NAME!` (also for a quoted name with a space, like "Ada Lovelace"), and make `bash greet.sh` with no name print `Hello, stranger!`. Tip: `edit greet.sh` opens the file in an editor.

mission.name: The Gatekeeper
mission.description: The nightly backup job has to know what a path is before it touches it: it crashed last night because a 'file' it was given turned out to be a directory.
mission.objective: Make `bash check_file.sh PATH` print `FILE` when PATH is a regular file, `DIR` when it is a directory, and `MISSING` when nothing exists there. In the MISSING case the script must exit with status 1. Paths may contain spaces (try `my notes.txt` and `old reports`).

mission.name: Bulk Renamer
mission.description: Every evening the reports in a drop folder must be marked as processed by renaming them from .txt to .bak. Somebody has been doing it by hand, one file at a time.
mission.objective: Make `bash rename.sh DIR` rename every file ending in `.txt` directly inside DIR to the same name ending in `.bak` (`q3 report.txt` becomes `q3 report.bak`). Other files and subdirectories stay as they are, and running it on a folder with no .txt files must change nothing and print no errors. incoming/ is there to try it on.

mission.name: DRY Deploy
mission.description: deploy.sh ships three services with three copy-pasted blocks. Next week a fourth service arrives, and nobody wants a fourth copy of the same lines.
mission.objective: Refactor deploy.sh so the steps for one service live in a single function `deploy_service NAME`, and the script calls it for api, web and worker. `bash deploy.sh` must print and copy exactly what it does now, and `deploy_service` must work for any service that has a build/NAME.tar.

mission.name: Config Parser
mission.description: The deploy pipeline keeps its settings in app.env, a KEY=value file filled in from a web form. Running `source app.env` broke on the first value with a space, and it would also run any $(command) somebody typed into the form.
mission.objective: Write load_env.sh so that `source load_env.sh FILE` exports every KEY=value line of FILE as an environment variable, with the value taken literally (spaces, `=` and `$(...)` kept as text, never run). Skip blank lines and lines starting with `#`, include the last line even if it has no newline, and print no errors. Try it with app.env.

mission.name: Fail Loudly
mission.description: safe_copy.sh puts a config into deploy/ without its comment lines. Yesterday it was given a file name with a typo: it printed `copy complete`, exited 0 and shipped an empty config. Last night someone ran it with no argument and it just sat there until the job timed out.
mission.objective: Harden safe_copy.sh: turn on bash strict mode (`set -euo pipefail`). With no argument it must print `SOURCE_FILE is required` to stderr and exit with status 1. A missing or unreadable source must make it fail (non-zero exit, no `copy complete`). A good source, even one with spaces in its name, must still be copied to deploy/app.conf without its comment lines.

mission.name: Parallel Launch
mission.description: The nightly maintenance runs three independent jobs one after another and takes three times longer than it needs to. Worse, when one job fails, nobody notices: the wrapper always reports success.
mission.objective: Write run_all.sh so that, run from its own folder, it starts ./task-a.sh, ./task-b.sh and ./task-c.sh at the same time, returns only after all three have finished, and exits with status 1 if any of them failed (0 if all succeeded). Right now one of the tasks fails, so try it and check `echo $?`.

mission.name: Template Engine
mission.description: Every environment needs its own app.conf, and people keep editing copies by hand and forgetting a port. The values live in vars.env; the config should be generated from them.
mission.objective: Write generate.sh so that, run in a folder containing vars.env, it creates app.conf there that looks exactly like app.conf.example but is filled in from whatever values vars.env holds. Build the file with a heredoc. Note the [logging] line: its `$` signs must stay as they are.

mission.name: What's My IP?
mission.description: A support ticket for the server app-07 came with the output of `ip addr` pasted in, and the network team wants a plain list of which IPv4 address sits on which interface.
mission.objective: From ip_addr.txt, write interfaces.txt with one line `INTERFACE ADDRESS` for every IPv4 address in the capture (address without the /prefix, interfaces with two addresses get two lines), in the order they appear. Interfaces without an IPv4 address are left out, and IPv6 addresses are ignored.

mission.name: Can You Hear Me?
mission.description: Before tonight's maintenance window you have to confirm which machines from the inventory are up. This sandbox has no network, so `./ping` stands in for ping: same output, same exit codes (0 = reply, 1 = no reply, 2 = unknown name).
mission.objective: Ping every host listed in hosts.txt with ./ping and write the names of the hosts that answer to reachable.txt, one per line (order does not matter). Comment and blank lines in hosts.txt are not hosts.

mission.name: What's Listening?
mission.description: A security review asks which TCP ports on web-03 can be reached from other machines. Someone ran `ss -tan` on it and saved the output to ss-output.txt.
mission.objective: Write exposed.txt: the TCP port numbers that web-03 is LISTENing on from other machines, one per line, each port once, sorted from low to high. A socket bound only to a loopback address (127.x.x.x or [::1]) is not reachable from outside and does not count; `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, `*` and the server's own addresses do.

mission.name: API Call
mission.description: The dashboards say metrics-api is unhealthy and you want the API's own opinion. It is running locally in this sandbox (its base URL is in api_url.txt, no internet needed), and the /health endpoint only answers clients that send the key from api.key.
mission.objective: Call the API's /health endpoint with curl, sending the key in an `X-API-Key` header, and save the value of `service.status` from the JSON reply to status.txt (just the word, without quotes).

mission.name: Name Resolution
mission.description: Before moving the internal services to a new network, the team needs every name in hosts.txt mapped to its current addresses. This sandbox has no DNS server, so `./dig` stands in for dig: same options and output format, answering from the internal zone.
mission.objective: Look up each name in hosts.txt with ./dig and write resolved.txt with one line `NAME ADDRESS` per IPv4 address (A record) the name finally resolves to. Follow CNAMEs to the address, give a name with two addresses two lines, and write `NAME NXDOMAIN` for a name that does not exist. Order does not matter.

mission.name: Connection Map
mission.description: web-03 (10.20.4.17) slowed down during the lunch peak and the on-call engineer suspects a single client is hogging connections. They saved `ss -tan` from that moment to connections.txt.
mission.objective: Find the remote address with the most ESTABLISHED connections to this server's HTTPS port (local port 443) and write `IP COUNT` on one line to top_talker.txt, for example `192.0.2.10 12`.

mission.name: Open Sesame
mission.description: TICKET.txt: the office can't reach the new admin UI on app-07 (tcp/8443), although someone already added a rule that allows it. The firewall is loaded at boot from firewall.rules, the output of `iptables-save`. (No root here, so you fix the file; iptables-restore would load it.)
mission.objective: Fix firewall.rules so that new connections from the office network 10.20.4.0/24 to tcp/8443 are accepted, while every other packet (8443 from anywhere else, the rest of 8000-8999, SSH, MySQL ...) is handled exactly as before. Keep the file loadable by iptables-restore (*filter ... COMMIT).

mission.name: Packet Sniff
mission.description: The IDS on web-03 (10.20.4.17) raised a 'possible port scan' alert, and someone left a 30-second packet capture of that moment in capture.pcap. Reading a saved capture with tcpdump needs no root.
mission.objective: Find the IP address that sent connection attempts (TCP SYN) to many different ports of web-03 and write it to scanner.txt. Then write the ports on web-03 that answered that address with SYN-ACK (meaning: open) to open_ports.txt, one per line, sorted from low to high.

mission.name: Service Down
mission.description: After last night's release myapp.service is down: it fails to start, and `systemctl enable` refuses to make it start at boot.
mission.objective: Fix etc/systemd/system/myapp.service so that myapp.service is enabled for multi-user.target and running (active). `./systemctl` is a mock that treats the sandbox as `/`: /etc/... means ./etc/... and /opt/... means ./opt/...

mission.name: Log Hunt
mission.description: myapp misbehaved after the 14:00 deploy. The on-call engineer wants every serious message it logged since then, and nothing else.
mission.objective: Save to errors.txt all journal entries of myapp.service with priority err or worse (err, crit, alert, emerg) logged since 14:00 today, oldest first, one per line as journalctl prints them. `./journalctl` is a mock of the real tool; its clock is frozen at 2024-04-08 14:30.

mission.name: Scheduled Sweep
mission.description: Upload temp files pile up on the app server. cleanup.sh deletes them, but nobody has scheduled it yet.
mission.objective: Add one job to crontab.txt that runs cleanup.sh (from this sandbox, by its absolute path) at 03:00 every weekday, Monday to Friday. Keep the existing lines of crontab.txt unchanged. crontab.txt is the file you would install with `crontab crontab.txt`.

mission.name: New Hire
mission.description: Dana Kim joins the platform team today and needs a login on the build server. Sam, already on the team, now also needs to run containers.
mission.objective: Create the user dana with a home directory /home/dana built from /etc/skel, login shell /bin/bash, full name "Dana Kim" and supplementary groups dev and docker. Add the existing user sam to docker without removing any of his current groups. The sandbox has real-format etc/passwd and etc/group files and mock ./useradd, ./usermod, ./userdel, ./id and ./groups tools that edit them like the real ones (no root needed).

mission.name: Controlled Power
mission.description: The CI pipeline logs in as the user deploy and runs deploy.sh, which fails at its sudo lines because sudo asks for a password nobody can type. Security will only sign off on the narrowest possible rule.
mission.objective: Create sudoers.d/deploy (the sandbox's /etc/sudoers.d) with a rule that lets deploy run, as root and without a password, exactly the two sudo commands in deploy.sh and nothing else. The file must pass `visudo -cf` and have the mode sudo expects for drop-in files (0440).

mission.name: Log Discipline
mission.description: The disk on the app server is 94% full: worker.log alone is 11G. A logrotate rule for myapp exists, but it only covers app.log and keeps everything uncompressed.
mission.objective: Fix logrotate.d/myapp (the sandbox's /etc/logrotate.d/myapp) so that one block covers every .log file in /var/log/myapp, rotates daily, keeps 14 old copies, compresses them, does not fail when a log is missing, and works for an app that never reopens its log files (see var/log/myapp/LISTING.txt).

mission.name: Env Surgery
mission.description: myapp will not start: start.sh loads its settings from .env, but app.sh keeps complaining about missing environment variables, and the shell prints strange 'command not found' errors.
mission.objective: Fix .env (leave start.sh and app.sh unchanged) so that sourcing it raises no errors and app.sh, started by ./start.sh, receives APP_MODE=production, APP_PORT=8080 and APP_NAME=My Shop.

mission.name: One-Shot Task
mission.description: A colleague queued the one-off cleanup.sh run for 03:30 tomorrow, right in the middle of the nightly backup. Change management approved tonight, 23:30, instead.
mission.objective: Leave the at queue with cleanup.sh (from this sandbox) queued exactly once, for tonight at 23:30, and no cleanup job at any other time. The unrelated certificate job must stay. ./at, ./atq and ./atrm are mocks of the real tools; their clock is frozen at Mon 2024-04-08 14:30.

mission.name: Pattern Mastery
mission.description: Security wants to know every host that touched the app today. The addresses are buried in app.log: after client=, with a :port, in [brackets], two on one line, next to version and build numbers that look a lot like IPs.
mission.objective: Write every distinct IPv4 address that appears in app.log to ips.txt, one address per line, each listed once (any order).

mission.name: Expense Report
mission.description: Finance exported last month's 200 expenses as expenses.csv and needs the spend per category for the budget meeting, biggest first. The export has a header row and a TOTAL footer row.
mission.objective: Write totals.txt with one line per category: the category name, a space, and the sum of its amounts with exactly two decimals (e.g. `meals 123.40`). Sort the lines by total, largest first.

mission.name: Config Injector
mission.description: The HTTPS site needs extra settings from /etc/myapp/extra.conf. app.conf has three server blocks, and each has a `# EXTRA CONFIG` placeholder, but only the HTTPS one (port 8443) may get the include.
mission.objective: In app.conf, add the line `include /etc/myapp/extra.conf;` directly after the `# EXTRA CONFIG` line of the `listen 8443` server block, and nowhere else. Every other line must stay as it is. Indent the new line however you like.

mission.name: JSON Surgeon
mission.description: The inventory API dumped its view of the platform to data.json: 30 services with nested status objects, and an owner with several contact entries. The incident template needs two facts from it.
mission.objective: Write report.txt with exactly two lines: `owner=<the owner's e-mail address>` and `active=<names of the services whose status.active is true, comma-separated, no spaces, in the order they appear in data.json>`.

mission.name: Quarantine Sweep
mission.description: A live API key (NEBULA_KEY) leaked into some of the 200 text files under files/. They must be moved out of the shared folders before the nightly sync, and some file names contain spaces and apostrophes.
mission.objective: Move every file under files/ that contains the exact text NEBULA_KEY into quarantine/ (directly, no subfolders), unchanged. Every other file stays where it is.

mission.name: Pretty Table
mission.description: The on-call handbook needs a readable inventory of services, but services.csv is a wall of commas, and its description column contains spaces.
mission.objective: Turn services.csv into table.txt: the same 15 lines (header included) with commas replaced by left-aligned columns separated by spaces (no tabs), each column starting at the same position on every line, and every value, including descriptions with spaces, kept whole.

mission.name: Lost on Login
mission.description: A new teammate added `export PROJECT_ROOT=/srv/projects/billing-api` to home/.profile on the build host, but neither SSH logins nor new terminal tabs ever see it. The account's dotfiles are in home/ (treat it as $HOME).
mission.objective: Fix the startup files in home/ so that PROJECT_ROOT=/srv/projects/billing-api is exported both in login shells (bash -l, like an SSH login) and in interactive non-login shells (bash -i, like a new terminal tab). Define the variable in exactly one of .bash_profile, .profile and .bashrc, and keep the existing login settings (EDITOR and ~/bin on PATH) and aliases working.

mission.name: Behind the Symlink
mission.description: A bad release is live and you are about to roll back. Step 1 of the runbook (deploy/RUNBOOK.txt): write down which directory deploy/current really is, because symlinks get swapped during a rollback.
mission.objective: Change into deploy/current. Save the path as the shell shows it through the symlink (absolute, ending in deploy/current) to logical.txt, and the real directory behind every symlink (absolute) to physical.txt. Both files go in the sandbox root, one path per file.

mission.name: report-.txt
mission.description: name-report.sh should write reports/report-<ENV>_<DAY>.txt, for example reports/report-staging_2026-11-09.txt. Instead every run produces reports/report-.txt or a name without the environment, and cron runs it without setting DAY at all.
mission.objective: Fix name-report.sh so that it writes reports/report-<ENV>_<DAY>.txt for whatever ENV and DAY it gets from the environment, with the same values on the 'environment:' and 'day:' lines inside the report. When DAY is unset or empty, use today's date in YYYY-MM-DD form. The script is checked with values you have not seen.

mission.name: Set But Not Seen
mission.description: Change ticket CHG-2207 (TICKET.txt) says to start the billing worker in production mode for a new region. Kim "set" APP_MODE and APP_REGION on the line before ./launcher.sh, yet the worker keeps starting in dev mode (shell-notes.txt shows what was typed).
mission.objective: Start the worker with ./launcher.sh so that it runs with the APP_MODE and APP_REGION from TICKET.txt. run.log, which launcher.sh writes and signs on every start, must show that production start. Do not change launcher.sh.

mission.name: Stale Helper
mission.description: deploy-helper keeps behaving like last year's version. The team's env.sh, which login shells and CI source, puts legacy/bin on PATH, while the current tools live in tools/bin. legacy/bin still holds report-legacy, which nobody has ported yet.
mission.objective: Fix env.sh so that after `source env.sh`, from any directory and in a fresh shell, deploy-helper runs the copy in tools/bin, report-legacy still runs from legacy/bin, and system commands (ls, grep, sort) still work. Every PATH entry env.sh adds must be an absolute directory (no empty, `.` or relative entries). Keep env.sh's other settings.

mission.name: Awkward Names

mission.name: Team Aliases

mission.name: Split the Streams
mission.description: nightly.sh prints its progress on stdout and its warnings and errors on stderr, and so far everything just scrolled past in a terminal. Ops wants it logged properly before the job moves to cron. Every run stamps its lines with a run id, so mixed-up logs are easy to spot.

mission.name: Missing Warnings
mission.description: The CI step `./build.sh | grep -c WARN` reports fewer warnings than anyone can see scrolling past, and the release dashboard shows every build as passed. The release manager wants real numbers before the go/no-go meeting (RELEASE-NOTES.txt).

Each file holds just the number. The test phase is flaky, so a second run gives different numbers.

mission.name: Three Copies
mission.description: Checkout errors are spiking (INCIDENT.txt). gen-events taps the live event bus and prints what passes by, one line per event; every run sees different traffic.

mission.name: Tenant Onboarding
mission.description: Ticket OPS-4521 lists the new tenants in tenants.txt, one per line, between comments and blank lines. Every tenant needs its own config directory before the platform team can switch them on. Last sprint, a quick `cat tenants.txt | xargs mkdir` created directories called `acme`, `corp` and `#`.

Comment lines (starting with #, also when indented) and blank lines are not tenants and must not produce anything. tenants/ must contain nothing else, and tenants.txt stays unchanged.

mission.name: Cron Clone
mission.description: report-gen builds the daily sales report. Run by hand it works, but every morning at 06:00 cron mails that there is no report (MAIL.txt). A test cron job saved the exact environment cron gives its jobs in cron.env.
mission.objective: 1) Run ./report-gen with exactly the environment in cron.env (nothing from your own shell) and save everything it prints, errors included, in cron-run.log. Do this before changing the script. 2) Then fix report-gen so that it exits 0 and writes a complete report (author in the header, a ruler line, the region totals) when started with only cron.env's variables. Leave cron.env as it is: it describes cron, not your fix.

mission.name: Ghost Config
mission.description: worker.env was corrected yesterday, but the DBA still sees the running worker connecting to the legacy database (TICKET.txt). Before anyone restarts it, prove what the live process is really using. (Linux only: this level reads /proc.)
mission.objective: For the running process started from bin/worker (not worker-metrics), write live.env with its actual DB_HOST, QUEUE and POOL, one KEY=value line each, and stale.txt with the names of the keys whose value in the running process differs from worker.env, one name per line. Don't stop or restart any process.
concepts: environment is fixed at exec time

mission.name: Clean Slate
mission.description: Someone sourced legacy-env.sh in a long-lived CI shell, and now curl goes through a dead proxy, grep colours its output and cd talks back. Opening a new shell is not an option there (NOTE.txt).
mission.objective: Write reset-env.sh so that `source reset-env.sh` removes from the current shell every variable and function that legacy-env.sh created and that can be removed: they must end up unset, not just empty, and `cd` must be the builtin again. It must not touch PATH or HOME, print no errors, never close the shell, and also be harmless in a shell where legacy-env.sh was never sourced. Write the name of the one thing that cannot be removed into readonly.txt.

mission.name: Workon
mission.description: The team's workon.sh is supposed to drop you into a project with its settings loaded. COMPLAINTS.txt: run as ./workon.sh it does nothing, sourced it only works from the repo root, and a typo in the project name closes the whole terminal. (Careful: that last one is real. Try the broken script in a throwaway shell such as `bash -c '...'`, not in this game shell; if it closes, type `reset`.)
mission.objective: Fix workon.sh so that `source /path/to/workon.sh NAME` works from any directory: it changes the caller's directory to projects/NAME and exports PROJECT=NAME plus the settings from that project's .project.env. For an unknown name it prints an error on stderr and returns a non-zero status, leaving the caller's shell open and unchanged. When it is run as a program instead of sourced, it exits non-zero with a message that mentions `source`.

mission.name: Glob Patrol
mission.description: ingest.sh loads the CSV uploads from incoming/. On quiet nights it crashes on a file literally called `incoming/*.csv`, it never sees the uploads in the dated subdirectories or the ones ending in .CSV, and last week it overwrote the summary.txt the auditors had signed off. (Needs bash 4 or newer: Linux, or ./play.sh --docker.)
mission.objective: Fix ingest.sh (it is tested with fresh upload directories you have not seen) so that it ingests every non-hidden file under incoming/, at any depth, whose name ends in .csv in any letter case; with no such files it ingests nothing and writes summary.txt with files=0 rows=0; and when summary.txt already exists it leaves it unchanged and exits with a non-zero status. Keep its output format.

mission.name: Gatekeeper
mission.description: guard.sh is the last check before a deploy: the pipeline runs `./guard.sh && ./deploy.sh`. Yesterday a release candidate went to production and a deploy with an empty DEPLOY_ENV went through, while the logs show lines like `[: too many arguments`. Meanwhile a perfectly good v1.4.0 was refused.
mission.objective: Fix guard.sh so that it follows RULES.txt for every possible value of DEPLOY_ENV and RELEASE (unset, empty, with spaces, with * or other odd characters): exit 0 when the deploy may go ahead, exit 1 when it must stop, and never let bash print an error. It is tested with many inputs you have not seen, run in a directory full of files.
concepts: exit status 2 of a failed test

mission.name: Which Deploy?
mission.description: On the jump host, typing `deploy` runs a different program depending on the terminal: SSH sessions get the old 1.4 hotfix binary, new tabs get a 2022 rsync script, and removing that alias only revealed yet another old version (TICKET.txt). The jump host's home directory is home/ in this sandbox.
mission.objective: Change the startup files under home/ so that in every new shell started with HOME=home/, both login shells (bash -l) and terminal tabs (bash -i), `deploy` is the program tools/bin/deploy (type -t says file, command -v gives that path). Keep opt/deploy-1.4 and scripts/deploy-legacy.sh on disk, keep PATH's system directories, and keep the team shortcuts ll, gs and mkcd working in terminal tabs.

mission.name: DSN Splitter
mission.description: The app reads its database settings from db.env, which parse-dsn.sh writes from a DSN out of the secrets vault. Since the vault switched to generated passwords, every db.env comes out empty or broken. Some examples are in dsns.txt.
mission.objective: Fix parse-dsn.sh so that `./parse-dsn.sh 'scheme://user:password@host[:port]/dbname'` writes db.env in the current directory, and `source db.env` then sets DB_USER, DB_PASS, DB_HOST, DB_PORT (5432 when the DSN has none) and DB_NAME to exactly the DSN's parts. Passwords may contain @, :, $, # and spaces; user names and host names never contain @ or :. Use only shell variables: no temporary files. It is tested with DSNs you have not seen.
concepts: pipes run read in a subshell

mission.name: Newcomer Bootstrap
mission.description: Onboarding runs bootstrap.sh for every new team member to set up their shell (ONBOARDING.txt). The draft a teammate left behind writes the wrong things: some values are frozen that should be looked up at login, some are left as variables that should have been filled in, and every rerun piles up another copy.
mission.objective: Fix bootstrap.sh so that, run as `TEAM=... OWNER="..." ./bootstrap.sh` for a newcomer's $HOME, it writes ~/.config/team.env with TEAM and OWNER fixed to the values given (OWNER may contain a space), adds a team block to the existing ~/.bashrc (keeping what is there) that puts this repo's tools/bin, as an absolute path, in front of the PATH the shell started with, defines an alias mine that runs `teamctl list --owner "$USER"` with $USER of the shell where it is used, and exports TEAM and OWNER from team.env, and makes ~/.bash_profile read ~/.bashrc so login shells get the same. A second run must change no file. It is tested with a fresh home and random values.

mission.name: Ship the Site
mission.description: The build pipeline left the finished website in build/dist/site/. The release engineer wants it as release-2.3.tar.gz, and the deploy script unpacks it with a plain `tar -xzf release-2.3.tar.gz` on the web server, expecting one site/ directory to appear.

Every member must be inside a top-level site/ directory (site/index.html, not build/dist/site/index.html, not index.html), and it must hold every file of build/dist/site/, hidden ones included, and nothing else. Leave build/ as it is.

mission.name: Just the Nginx Config
mission.description: Someone broke the nginx config on web-04 and the only good copy is in last night's full backup etc-backup.tar.gz, about 2,000 files of /etc. Unpacking all of it would only add noise; you need just the nginx directory.
mission.objective: Extract only the etc/nginx directory from etc-backup.tar.gz into restore/, so that restore/etc/nginx/ is exactly the copy from the backup (all files and links) and nothing else ends up in restore/. Do not change etc-backup.tar.gz.

mission.name: Disk at 92%
mission.description: The monitoring alert says /var on shop-02 is 92% full. In logs/ the app's rotated logs app.log.2 to app.log.12 were never compressed because the logrotate job broke. Logrotate runs with delaycompress: app.log is the file the app is writing right now, and app.log.1 stays plain for one more day.
mission.objective: In logs/, compress app.log.2 through app.log.12 with gzip, so that each one becomes app.log.N.gz with the same content and no uncompressed copy is left. app.log and app.log.1 must stay exactly as they are (same file, same content), and the old app.log.13.gz and app.log.14.gz stay unchanged.

mission.name: Partner Drop
mission.description: A logistics partner drops gzipped CSV exports into inbox/ every night. The import job reads plain .csv files from import/, and the compliance team wants the original .gz files left in inbox/ exactly as they arrived, for the audit trail.
mission.objective: For every inbox/NAME.csv.gz, create import/NAME.csv with its uncompressed content (one CSV per .gz file, same names). Leave inbox/ exactly as it was: all .gz files still there and unchanged, and no uncompressed files in it. import/ must contain only those CSVs.

mission.name: Legacy Transfer
mission.description: The auditors' old transfer system only accepts bzip2 files. A colleague already put outbox/ledger-2025.tar.bz2 there, but the system rejected it (see outbox/transfer-rejected.txt). It checks what the file really is, not its name.
mission.objective: Put two real bzip2 files in outbox/: ledger-2025.tar.bz2, a bzip2-compressed tar of the ledger/ directory (members ledger/..., all its files), and audit.log.bz2, the bzip2-compressed audit.log. Keep audit.log itself where it is, and do not change ledger/.

mission.description: The nightly import crashed halfway with 'bunzip2: Data integrity error'. The database dumps came from the old server as dumps/*.sql.bz2, and at least one of them was damaged on the way. Nobody knows which.
mission.objective: Move every damaged .sql.bz2 file from dumps/ into quarantine/ (unchanged), and for every intact one write its uncompressed dump to restore/NAME.sql. Leave the intact .bz2 files in dumps/. restore/ must hold only complete, correct .sql files.

mission.description: Today is 2026-11-10. logs/ on the reporting server holds one log per day since May (app-YYYY-MM-DD.log), and the retention policy says: everything older than the current month goes into one xz-compressed tar per month, and the plain files go away only after the archive has been checked.
mission.objective: Create archive/2026-05.tar.xz, archive/2026-06.tar.xz ... archive/2026-10.tar.xz (six xz-compressed tar files, nothing else in archive/). Each one must hold exactly the daily logs whose file NAME carries that month, with unchanged content. Then remove those archived logs from logs/. The November logs stay in logs/, plain and unchanged.

mission.name: Size Before You Unpack
mission.description: Five database exports arrived as exports/*.sql.xz. Before anyone unpacks them on the small staging volume, ops wants the exact total uncompressed size in bytes for the capacity ticket. The first one needed is the customers table.

Then restore exports/customers.sql (its uncompressed content). Keep all five .xz files unchanged, and do not leave any other uncompressed export in exports/.

mission.description: Every week the client gets handover.zip, a zip of the handover/ folder. Last week's zip is still here, and their portal identifies it by its archive comment, so it has to be refreshed in place rather than built from scratch. Since last week, files in handover/ were changed, added and deleted, and docs/latest now points to the v4 release notes.

The archive comment that is in handover.zip now must still be there. Do not change handover/.

mission.description: A customer uploaded upload.zip from their Mac. It has CSV files scattered over several folders, plus documentation, images and Mac metadata. The importer reads import/ and does not look into subfolders. import/customers.csv is already there and was corrected by hand yesterday; it is newer than the copy in the zip.
mission.objective: Put every real .csv file from upload.zip into import/, directly (no subdirectories), with its content from the zip. Nothing else from the zip goes into import/: no other file types, no Mac metadata files. import/customers.csv must stay exactly as it is now. Do not change upload.zip.

mission.name: Inside the initrd
mission.description: A server boots into the initramfs shell instead of its root filesystem. Before rebuilding anything, the team wants to know which kernel modules the current initrd.img actually ships, and what configuration it carries in etc/. The file is a gzip-compressed cpio archive in the newc format, like most Linux initramfs images.
mission.objective: Write modules.txt with the file name of every kernel module (*.ko) inside initrd.img, one per line, file names only (e.g. nvme.ko, no directories). Then extract only the etc/ tree of the image into initrd-root/, so initrd-root/etc/ matches the image and nothing else from it is unpacked anywhere. Do not change initrd.img.

mission.name: Five Megabytes Max
mission.description: The vendor needs last night's db-backup.tar.gz (about 23 MB), but their file share rejects any upload larger than 5 MB, and their ticket says exactly what that means: 5,000,000 bytes. They will glue the pieces together with `cat db-backup.tar.gz.part-* > db-backup.tar.gz` and then check it with `sha256sum -c db-backup.sha256`.
mission.objective: Fill outgoing/ with the upload: the backup cut into pieces named db-backup.tar.gz.part-aa, db-backup.tar.gz.part-ab, ... (each at most 5,000,000 bytes, and joined in name order they give back the exact original), plus db-backup.sha256, a checksum file that passes `sha256sum -c` for the rebuilt db-backup.tar.gz in the vendor's folder. Nothing else in outgoing/. Keep db-backup.tar.gz unchanged in the sandbox root.

mission.name: Fourteen Pieces

mission.name: Mirror, Mirror
mission.description: mirror-03 serves installer images from isos/. Upstream's SHA256SUMS lists twelve images, but we only download the six our installers use, and the storage team suspects one of them was damaged on the way in. MIRROR-NOTES.txt has the house rules.

Then write isos/SHA256SUMS.local with the sha256 of exactly the image files (.iso, .img) still in isos/, so that `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.local` passes when run inside isos/.

mission.name: Seeing Double
mission.description: Five devices were synced into photos/ at the same time, so the same picture often arrived several times under different names (see INTAKE.txt). 400 files, and nobody knows how many distinct pictures.

mission.name: What's in a Name
mission.description: 80 chunks were carved out of the crashed upload volume into recovered/. The carver guessed their extensions, mostly wrong, and some chunks have none (RECOVERY-NOTES.txt). The upload service needs them sorted by what they really are.
mission.objective: Move every chunk from recovered/ to sorted/<type>/chunk-NNN.<type>, where <type> is its real content: gz, bz2, xz, zip, tar, tar.gz (a gzip that holds a tar archive), png, pdf or txt. Zero-byte chunks go to sorted/empty/chunk-NNN with no extension. Keep the content unchanged and leave nothing in recovered/.

mission.name: Time and Permission
mission.description: The acme-agent installer refuses the extracted bundle: the vendor's MANIFEST pins the mode and mtime of every path, and some entries drifted during extraction (INSTALLER-ERROR.txt). Several names contain spaces, and lib/ holds a symlink.
mission.objective: First write drift.txt in the sandbox root: one line per MANIFEST path whose mode or mtime differs, written exactly as in MANIFEST. Then fix the bundle so every entry (the symlink itself included) has exactly the mode and mtime MANIFEST gives, without changing anything else.

mission.name: Dead Weight
mission.description: projects/ is going to cold storage, and the archive should not carry caches that any build can recreate (ARCHIVE-PLAN.txt). First the team wants to see which cache dirs are worth excluding.
mission.objective: Write bloat.txt in the sandbox root: one line 'KiB<TAB>path' for every directory named node_modules, .cache, target or build under projects/ that uses more than 5 MiB (5120 KiB) on disk, sorted largest first. Size = what `du -sk` reports for that dir, path relative like projects/app/build. Only the outermost cache dir counts: skip cache dirs that sit inside another cache dir. Don't delete anything.

mission.name: Will It Fit
mission.description: The catalog restore.tar.xz has to be unpacked into /srv on every kiosk that can take it (RESTORE-TICKET.txt). You can't log in to the kiosks; all you have is last night's df -PT and df -i output of each one in hosts/.
mission.objective: Write targets.txt with the names of the hosts (file names in hosts/ without .txt, one per line) that can take the restore: the filesystem that holds /srv on that host must have at least as many free KiB as the uncompressed size of restore.tar.xz (the tar inside, in KiB rounded up) and at least as many free inodes as the archive has members (files and directories).

mission.name: Needle in a Gzip Stack
mission.description: Support needs the full history of order 88412 (TICKET.txt). Its log lines are spread over two weeks of rotated logs in logs/: app.log, app.log.1, then compressed rotations, some gzip, some bzip2, some xz. The disk is almost full, so nothing gets unpacked.
mission.objective: Write order-88412.txt with every log line whose order= field is exactly 88412, from all files in logs/, oldest first, as plain log lines (no file names in front). Leave every file in logs/ as it is and don't write decompressed copies anywhere.

mission.name: Pack Light
mission.description: orders-api 2.4.0 is ready to ship. The release tarball is built from the working copy in app/, which also holds a git repo, node_modules, log files and production secrets (RELEASE-CHECKLIST.txt).
mission.objective: Create release.tar.gz in the sandbox root, gzip-compressed, with members starting with app/. It must contain every file of app/ except: the .git directory and .gitignore, every node_modules directory (at any depth), every *.log file, and every file named exactly .env. .env.example files, logs/.keep and .github/ must be included. Don't change app/.

mission.name: Week of Incrementals
mission.description: Capstone. data/ gets a full backup on Sunday and incremental backups Monday to Wednesday (BACKUP-PLAN.txt). It is Sunday evening; ./simulate-day.sh plays each next day, and on Thursday the data disk dies. Needs GNU tar (Linux).
mission.objective: Take backups/data-sun.tar.gz (full) now, then after each of ./simulate-day.sh mon, tue and wed take backups/data-mon.tar.gz, data-tue.tar.gz and data-wed.tar.gz: gzip-compressed GNU incremental archives that hold only what changed. Then run ./simulate-day.sh thu and restore Wednesday's state into restored/, so that restored/data is exactly data/ as it was on Wednesday night, with files deleted during the week absent.

mission.name: Five Generations
mission.description: Capstone. Cron should run ./rotate.sh every night to keep five generations of the bakery's site backup (ROTATION.txt). Kim's draft of rotate.sh was never tested, and someone already deleted backups/site.tar.gz.3 by hand.
mission.objective: Make rotate.sh (executable, run from the sandbox root) keep backups/site.tar.gz.1 (newest) ... .5 (oldest): each run drops .5, moves every existing generation up by one (a missing one leaves its gap moving up too) and creates a fresh .1, a gzip tar of site/. It must exit 0, also when generations are missing, and leave nothing else in backups/. The check runs a copy of your script many times in a scratch folder.

mission.name: Trust, but Verify
mission.description: Capstone. A vendor's delivery/ holds eight archives and a SHA256SUMS file. Some names lie about the format, and the security team warns that at least one archive was tampered with and that archives can try to write outside the folder they are unpacked in (INTAKE-POLICY.txt).
mission.objective: Write audit.csv: the header name,real_type,members,checksum_ok,unsafe, then one row per archive with its file name, its real format (tar, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar.xz or zip), the number of entries it lists (directories included), yes/no for matching SHA256SUMS, and yes/no for having a member path that is absolute or contains a .. component. Then extract every archive that matches its checksum and is safe into accepted/<name>/ (name = file name up to the first dot), and nothing else. No file may be written outside its accepted/ folder.

mission.name: Invoices for Legal
mission.description: Legal is preparing for an audit and wants a copy of every invoice PDF on the old shared drive. The dump in share/ grew for ten years without rules: Invoice_2026-03.PDF sits next to 'invoice - april.pdf', and templates, backups and receipts are mixed in.
mission.objective: Write the path of every file under share/ whose name contains the word invoice and ends in .pdf, both in any letter case, to invoices.txt (one path per line, like share/Finance/x.pdf or ./share/Finance/x.pdf). Nothing else goes in the list; do not change share/.

mission.name: After the Failed Deploy
mission.description: Last night's deploy died halfway through. Before anyone cleans up releases/, the on-call engineer wants two lists for the incident ticket: every symbolic link under releases/ (some point at shared folders, one may point at nothing) and every directory the deploy left completely empty.
mission.objective: Write links.txt with the path of every symbolic link under releases/, and empty-dirs.txt with the path of every empty directory under releases/ (one path per line, like releases/x or ./releases/x). A directory that holds anything, even a hidden file, is not empty. Do not change releases/.

mission.name: Too Big to Send
mission.description: The mail relay rejects every attachment larger than 10 MiB (10 x 1024 x 1024 bytes), and a crashed upload left zero-byte attachments behind. Messages in outbox/ keep bouncing, and support wants to tell each sender which file to fix.
mission.objective: Write oversize.txt with the path of every file under outbox/ that is larger than 10 MiB, and empty.txt with the path of every file under outbox/ that is 0 bytes (one path per line, like outbox/x or ./outbox/x). Files of exactly 10 MiB are still allowed. Do not change outbox/.

mission.name: What Changed Last Night
mission.description: The shop went down an hour ago and the first question in the incident channel is the usual one: which configs were touched recently? etc/ is a copy of the server's /etc with the original timestamps.
mission.objective: Write recent.txt with the path of every file under etc/ whose content was modified during the last 24 hours (one path per line, like etc/x or ./etc/x). Only files, not directories. Do not change anything in etc/.

mission.name: Compress the Old Logs
mission.description: app/logs fills the disk every few weeks because nobody configured rotation. Until logrotate is set up, ops wants the old logs compressed in place, with a single find command that can later go into cron.
mission.objective: Compress (gzip, in place, so x.log becomes x.log.gz with the same content) every file under app/logs whose name ends in .log and that was last modified more than 7 days ago. Logs modified within the last 7 days stay as they are, and no other file is compressed or changed.

mission.name: Leaked Keys
mission.description: Security found a paste with 40 of our API keys and saved them in leaked.txt, one per line. Before rotating them, they need to know which requests in logs/ were made with any of those keys. The keys contain characters like . + * and $.
mission.objective: Write hits.txt with every log line under logs/ that contains any of the keys from leaked.txt exactly as written, each prefixed with its file name the way grep prints it with several files (logs/dir/file.log:the whole line). No line numbers, no other lines. Do not change logs/.

mission.name: Root Over SSH
mission.description: An auditor asks which of our 12 servers let root log in over SSH with a password. Copies of their sshd configs are in hosts/<host>/sshd_config, edited by hand for years: commented-out lines, tabs, odd capitalisation, and settings that appear twice.
mission.objective: Write root-login-hosts.txt with the names of the hosts (the folder names under hosts/, one per line, any order) where sshd's effective PermitRootLogin setting is yes. Values like prohibit-password, without-password, forced-commands-only and no do not allow password logins, and a host without the setting uses the default, prohibit-password.

mission.name: What Is Actually Set
mission.description: A database is slow and the vendor asks for 'your effective postgresql.conf, without the comments'. Ours is the stock file of about 600 lines, edited over the years: commented defaults, indented comment lines, blank lines with stray spaces and tabs, and a few dozen real settings, some with a comment after the value.
mission.objective: Create effective.conf containing exactly the lines of postgresql.conf that are settings: drop every line that is empty, contains only spaces/tabs, or whose first non-blank character is #. Keep the remaining lines unchanged (including any # comment after a value) and in their original order. postgresql.conf itself must stay unchanged.

mission.name: The Noisiest Services
mission.description: Error budgets are reviewed tomorrow. logs/ holds today's log of each of our 30 services (logs/<service>.log, one line per event, the level in the second column). The SRE lead wants the services that logged more than 50 ERROR lines today.
mission.objective: Write noisy.txt with one line '<file> <count>' (for example 'billing.log 73') for every log in logs/ that has more than 50 lines with the level ERROR, sorted by count, highest first. Other levels never count, even when their message mentions something like NOERROR.

mission.name: Who Killed the Worker
mission.description: The image worker crashed 15 times overnight. A FATAL line never names the request it was working on, but the line just before each crash always carries that request's req=<id>. The developers want the ids so they can replay those requests.
mission.objective: Write fatal-reqs.txt with the request id (only the id, without req=) from the line directly before each FATAL in worker.log, one per line, in the order they occur in the log. When several FATAL lines follow each other, they belong to the request on the line before the first of them, which is listed once. Do not change worker.log.

mission.name: Columns for Two Audiences
mission.description: The asset database exported assets.tsv: tab-separated, a header line, 14 columns, and some values (models, rooms, notes) contain spaces. Ops wants a short list for the rack audit, and the hardware vendor needs the full export without our staff's e-mail addresses.
mission.objective: Create inventory.tsv with the columns serial, hostname, rack in exactly that order, and vendor.tsv with all columns of assets.tsv except owner_email, in their original order. Both keep the header line, every row of assets.tsv, and tabs between the fields. assets.tsv must stay unchanged.

mission.name: Three Exports, One Report
mission.description: The monitoring tool can only export one metric per file: hosts.txt, cpu.txt and mem.txt, one value per line, all in the same host order. cpu.txt came from the Windows reporting box. The team wants a single table, and the CPU-saturated hosts as a list for `ansible --limit`.
mission.objective: Create report.tsv with one line per host: host, cpu, mem separated by tabs, in the order of hosts.txt, no header. Create limit.txt with one single line: the hosts whose cpu is 90 or more, joined with commas (web-03,db-01,...), in report order, without spaces or a trailing comma. Leave the three input files unchanged.

mission.name: Whose Laptop Is That?
mission.description: The office network has devices nobody recognises. The DHCP server's lease file dnsmasq.leases (expiry mac ip hostname client-id) says which MAC got which IP; the asset inventory inventory.csv (MAC,owner,team, with a header) says who owns which MAC. The two systems write MAC addresses differently.
mission.objective: Write owners.txt with one line 'ip mac owner' for every lease in dnsmasq.leases: the MAC as the lease file writes it, the owner from inventory.csv, or UNKNOWN when the inventory has no entry for that MAC. Sort the lines by IP address numerically (10.20.0.9 before 10.20.0.10).

mission.name: Twin Servers Drift
mission.description: web-1 and web-2 sit behind the same load balancer and should be identical, but a deploy works on one and fails on the other. You have both package lists as dumped by the inventory agent: web1.pkgs and web2.pkgs (package<TAB>version, in install order). The two dumps were taken with different formats: web-1 adds the architecture to some names (libc6:amd64), web-2 never does.
mission.objective: Write only-web1.txt with the names of the packages installed on web-1 but not on web-2, and only-web2.txt with those installed on web-2 but not on web-1. One package name per line, each name once, without architecture or version. A package installed on both hosts in different versions is not drift.

mission.name: Capacity Review
mission.description: For the quarterly capacity review, the team wants the host inventory grouped by datacenter, busiest hosts first. inventory.txt (host dc rack load mem, with a header line) comes from a metrics exporter that writes some loads in scientific notation, like 1e-02 or 1.2e+01.
mission.objective: Write sorted.txt: the header line first, then every row of inventory.txt unchanged, ordered by datacenter (alphabetically), then by load as a number (highest first), then by host name in natural order (web9 before web10).
concepts: keeping a header out of sort

mission.name: Is It Beaconing?
mission.description: A laptop was quarantined after an antivirus alert. Malware often phones home by looking up the same odd domain again and again. You have two hours of the laptop's local DNS cache log, dnsmasq.log: every lookup is a query[...] line, followed by forwarded/reply or cached lines for the same name. Applications write names in any case, and some add a trailing dot (example.com.).
mission.objective: Count the query[...] lines per domain, treating names case-insensitively and ignoring a trailing dot. Write beacons.txt with one line 'count domain' for every domain queried 3 times or more, highest count first, and once.txt with every domain queried exactly once, one per line. Write domains in lowercase without the trailing dot.

mission.name: Usernames From HR
mission.description: 64 people start next month and HR sent their names in newhires.txt, exported from a Windows tool. Accounts are created from a list of usernames, and the naming rule is: all lowercase, name parts joined by an underscore (Mary J. Smith becomes mary_j_smith). The export separates name parts with spaces, double spaces or tabs, initials have dots, and some names are in capitals.
mission.objective: Write usernames.txt with one username per line, in the same order as newhires.txt: the name in lowercase, with every space, tab and dot turned into an underscore and runs of underscores squeezed into one. No carriage returns (\r) may remain.

mission.name: Serial Console Cleanup
mission.description: A database server failed to mount its backup share after a reboot. The datacenter tech captured the serial console (boot messages and a short login session) in console.raw for the incident ticket, but the capture is full of carriage returns, NUL padding bytes, terminal bells and ANSI colour codes, and the ticket system shows it as garbage.
mission.objective: Write console.txt: the text of console.raw, line by line, with every carriage return (\r), NUL byte, bell character (\a) and ANSI colour sequence (ESC [ ... m) removed. Everything else stays exactly as it is, including the tabs in the /etc/hosts lines and the empty lines.

mission.name: Vendor Ticket
mission.description: The vendor of the orders API asks for two things for their support ticket: the database settings from app.ini and the part of trace.log their crash tool pointed at, lines 1200 to 1260. app.ini has several sections, including a [database-replica] section that is not the one they want.
mission.objective: Write db-section.txt with the [database] section of app.ini: from its [database] header line up to, but not including, the next section header, every line unchanged. Write excerpt.txt with lines 1200 to 1260 of trace.log (both included), unchanged.

mission.name: CDN Cutover
mission.description: Marketing moves its static files to a new CDN tonight and wants ISO dates on the site at the same time. The 40 HTML templates in templates/ (and templates/emails/) still load everything from http://old-cdn.example.com/ and print dates as DD/MM/YYYY. Some templates also link to our print partner, whose domain is old-cdn-example.com; those links must stay.
mission.objective: Edit the templates in place: every http://old-cdn.example.com/<path> becomes https://cdn.example.net/v2/<path>, and every date written DD/MM/YYYY becomes YYYY-MM-DD. Nothing else may change (old-cdn-example.com links included), and no backup files may be left in templates/.

mission.name: Who Is Eating The Web Server?
mission.description: The shop's web server swapped all night and the load average stays high even though traffic is low. Before rebooting, the on-call engineer saved a snapshot of `ps aux` in ps-aux.txt (about 900 processes). Two questions: which web workers (user www-data) use too much memory, and which processes are stuck (state D, uninterruptible I/O) or dead but not reaped (state Z, zombie)?
mission.objective: Write heavy.txt with one line 'PID COMMAND' for every process of user www-data whose %MEM is more than 5, and stuck.txt with one line 'PID COMMAND' for every process whose state (STAT) is D or Z, whatever flags follow the letter. COMMAND is the complete command line with all its arguments. Keep the order of ps-aux.txt.

mission.name: Logfmt To CSV
mission.description: The new tracing dashboard imports CSV, but the shop's services log in logfmt: app.log has lines of key=value pairs such as ts=... level=info svc=api msg="request done" dur=850ms, with the keys in any order. Durations are written in microseconds (us), milliseconds (ms) or seconds (s), and some lines have no dur at all.
mission.objective: Write slow.csv: the header line ts,svc,dur_ms, then one line ts,svc,dur_ms for every log line whose dur= value is more than 500 milliseconds, in the order of app.log. ts and svc are copied from the ts= and svc= keys; dur_ms is the duration in milliseconds as a whole number, rounded (1.2s becomes 1200). Other keys that merely contain those names (db_dur, upstream_svc) are not the ones you want.

mission.name: NAS Storage Bill
mission.description: The NAS is 92% full and management wants to charge storage back to its users. Someone already ran find /nas -printf '%p\t%u\t%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td\n' > files.lst 2>&1, so files.lst has one line per file: path, owner, size in bytes and last-modified date, separated by tabs. Paths contain spaces, a few files are tens of GiB, and the find errors went into the file too.
mission.objective: Write usage.txt with one line per user: the user name, the total size of their files in GiB (1 GiB = 1024^3 bytes), and the size of their files last modified before 2025-01-01 in GiB, separated by tabs, both numbers with exactly two decimals (e.g. amira<TAB>812.34<TAB>401.20). Sort the lines by total GiB, largest first.

mission.name: Weekly Bounce Report
mission.description: Every Monday the mail team asks which customers' mailings bounce the most, so they can warn them before the relays land on a blocklist. The logs of both relays are under var/log/ (rotated daily, older ones gzipped). Postfix writes the sender of a message (from=) and its delivery result (status=) on different lines, linked by the queue ID. Some bounces come from the empty sender <> (bounce notices that bounced themselves).
mission.objective: From every mail.log* file under var/log/ (any depth, plain or .gz) modified in the last 7 days, count the bounced messages (status=bounced) per sender domain: the part after @ in the message's from=<...>, in lowercase; messages from the empty sender <> don't count. Write report.txt with the top 5 as lines 'rank domain count' (e.g. '1 example.org 17'): highest count first, equal counts ordered by domain name. Don't change or unpack the logs.
concepts: awk arrays as a join on a key

Leave the packaged unit file and report.service unchanged, and keep report.service enabled and running. `systemctl` and `journalctl` are mocks that treat the sandbox as `/` (packaged units are in ./usr/lib/systemd/system, local ones in ./etc/systemd/system) and behave like the real tools.

Don't change the captures.

mission.name: When the Box Is Idle
